complete_examples.text: As suggested by Shan et al. [24], the static strength can be calculated by the effective consolidation stress theory (18) where qfis the undrained shear strength; ccu and φcu are the cohesion and internal friction angle of the subgrade soil, respectively; K0 is the lateral pressure coefficient of the subgrade soil; σcz is the gravitational stress of the subgrade soil.

According to the effective consolidation stress theory presented by Shen (2000), the undrained shear strength of cohesive soil only depends on the effective stress in the consolidation state before rupture, because the development of soil from the consolidation state to the damage state is relatively fast, and the change of moisture content and strength is small.
